title: Lawmakers hear about one company's nuclear fusion plans in New Mexico

content:
NEW MEXICO (KRQE) – New Mexico has been investing in nuclear fusion, but what does the future of the energy technology look like for the state? On Thursday, lawmakers heard from an expert from one fusion company on what their plans include.

Story continues below

Matt Pahl with Pacific Fusion told New Mexico lawmakers that investing in fusion energy is important for the state's future. "Fusion has the ability to provide affordable, reliable, on-demand power that's carbon-free using inexpensive, nearly limitless fuel," said Pahl.

The energy company broke ground on a fusion demonstration facility in Albuquerque's Mesa del Sol last month. Fusion works similarly to how the sun works, using intense heat energy to merge the nuclei of two atoms into one, emitting energy in the process. On Thursday, Pahl touted fusion energy's low waste. "And it does not use uranium or plutonium, which is notable just for resource consideration, and particularly in New Mexico, given our history with uranium mining," said Pahl.

Pahl said that once fusion is implemented, it's projected to decarbonize the state's grid and save money. "And what we found is that not only does fusion reduce carbon faster than the status quo for the utility right now, but it also provides savings for ratepayers. In this analysis, it was to the tune of nearly $850 million," said Pahl.

Pahl said Pacific Fusion is also set to hire 200 permanent employees through their research and manufacturing campus and up to 200 other operational jobs when the first power system is built.

But not all lawmakers are onboard. Democratic Senator William Soules (D-Doña Anas) said state money might be better invested into proven energy sources like solar and wind. "Why are we not putting more money and effort into those as opposed to an unproven technology that, mind you, may be the holy grail into the future, but I think you made two comments, one 10 to 20 years out," said Sen. Soules.

Pacific Fusion also mentioned that they hope to have carbon-free and on-demand power ready by the mid-2030s.
